findings.current: I was already prepared for this when I told you to spare the men guarding the underground prison.
findings.defect: The draft omits that the prison guards were Baeksang’s subordinates, weakening the hierarchy and the Beast Miao King’s reason for anticipating Baeksang’s response.
findings.rationale: 네 수하들 explicitly means “your subordinates,” not merely unidentified men.
findings.replacement: I was already prepared for this when I told you to spare your subordinates guarding the underground prison.
findings.source: 뇌옥을 지키던 네 수하들을 살려 두라 말했을 때부터 이미 각오하고 있었다.

findings.current: They grumbled with their mouths, but their eyes were smiling.
findings.defect: The draft assigns the grumbling and smiling to the gathered warriors, but the subject in context is Wonhu.
findings.rationale: The sentence is framed by Wonhu’s dialogue and the following clause in which Wonhu passes around the gourd; the singular implicit subject remains Wonhu.
findings.replacement: Though Wonhu grumbled, his eyes were smiling.

findings.current: Good grief. Did they gather nothing but dogs here? Why do you all have such sharp noses?
findings.defect: Rendering 개새끼들 as neutral “dogs” sanitizes the insult and weakens the crude dog-and-sharp-noses joke.
findings.rationale: 개새끼들 is strongly insulting while also supplying the literal canine image needed for the nose joke.
findings.replacement: Hell, did they round up nothing but a pack of fucking mutts? Why are all your noses so sharp?
findings.source: 허어, 개새끼들만 모아 놨나. 왜 이리들 코가 좋아?

findings.current: So this is what I find out? You aren’t dogs. You’re all just a bunch of braggarts.
findings.defect: The payoff again neutralizes 개새끼들 and reads as though Wonhu had literally mistaken the men for dogs.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves both the vulgar register and the callback to Wonhu’s earlier canine insult.
findings.replacement: Turns out you aren’t fucking mutts after all—just a bunch of blowhards.
findings.source: 이거 알고 보니, 개새끼들이 아니라 순 허풍쟁이들이었군.

findings.current: We both know what’s going on, so why bother? Go gnaw on a tiger’s dick.
findings.defect: “Gnaw on” changes the deliberately absurd action in the insult, which tells the listener to peel and eat it.
findings.rationale: 까 잡수쇼 retains both the peeling action and the sarcastically polite command to eat.
findings.replacement: We both know what’s going on, so why bother? Go peel and eat a tiger’s dick.
findings.source: 다 아는 처지에 뭘. 호랑이 좆이나 까 잡수쇼.

findings.current: His skin was so pale that the word *white* seemed entirely appropriate.
findings.defect: The description reverses which adjective is being judged appropriate: the source says his starkly white skin merits the description “pallid,” not that pale skin merits the word “white.”
findings.rationale: 창백하다는 표현이 어울릴 만큼 makes “pallid” the resulting characterization of his exceptionally white skin.
findings.replacement: His skin was so starkly white that *pallid* was the only word for it.
findings.source: 창백하다는 표현이 어울릴 만큼 새하얀 피부.

findings.current: Even as the landscape rushed past us, there was not a single human shadow or a house of any unusual shape in sight. Nothing but grassland stretched in every direction.
findings.defect: The draft awkwardly makes the absence apply only to houses that might have unusual shapes and changes dense grassy undergrowth into open grassland.
findings.rationale: The source separately excludes people and the distinctively shaped houses, then says the surroundings are filled only with 풀숲, grassy thickets or undergrowth.
findings.replacement: Even as the landscape rushed past us, there was not a single person or one of the oddly shaped houses in sight—only thickets everywhere.
findings.source: 지금 이 순간에도 빠르게 스쳐 지나가는 풍경 속에는 사람의 그림자도, 여러 가지 독특한 형태를 띤 가옥(家屋)도 없었고 오직 풀숲만이 가득했다.

findings.current: No. It would be more accurate to say I had not been able to try.
findings.defect: The English is unnatural and does not clearly convey Taekyung’s emotional inability to bring himself to wake Yayul Mok.
findings.rationale: In context, 못했다 marks that Taekyung could not make himself attempt it because he knew Yayul Mok would try to return.
findings.replacement: No. It would be more accurate to say I couldn’t bring myself to try.
findings.source: 아니, 시도하지 못했다고 하는 것이 옳은 표현일 것이다.

findings.current: The scent pouch belonging to Yohi that I had discovered in the Western Region of Yeo.
findings.defect: The draft misnames the location as “Yeo,” introducing an unestablished place and severing its connection to Yohi’s Yao people.
findings.rationale: 요서부 refers to the western part of the Yao territory; the established ethnic name is Yao, not Yeo.
findings.replacement: The scent pouch belonging to Yohi that I had discovered in the western Yao territory.

summary: The draft contains one incorrect subject assignment, an omitted subordinate relationship, softened profanity and wordplay, several localized meaning shifts, and a misnamed location.
